cards.text: Israel is camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, about to cross into the promised land. The LORD speaks to Moses again, and this time it's about the Levites, the ones who do the work of the Tent of Meeting. Every other tribe gets a territory, but the Levites won't receive an inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23).

cards.question: The Levites won't get a territory of their own. So what does the LORD tell the other tribes to give them?

answers.text: Cities to live in with pasturelands
A strip of land by the Great Sea

cards.text: Then come the measurements, in cubits, from the city wall out on every side, with the city right in the center. EXACT numbers in every direction, and I'm over here measuring chocolate chips by "until it feels right."
Now here's where it gets interesting. Six of those Levite cities get a special job.

cards.question: Six of the Levites' cities are to be cities of ___, where a manslayer may flee.
On top of those six cities of refuge, the Levites get forty-two other cities. How many cities is that in all?

cards.text: Forty-eight cities have to come from somewhere. And some of these tribes are a LOT bigger than others.

cards.question: True or false: Every tribe gives the Levites the same number of cities, no matter how big the tribe is.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses that once Israel crosses the Jordan into Canaan, they're to set those cities of refuge apart. A city of refuge is a place to run to, so the question is, who's running?

cards.question: Who are the cities of refuge for?

answers.text: Someone who kills a person by accident
Someone who steals from a neighbor
Someone who can't pay back a debt

cards.text: These cities are a refuge from the avenger. This man is running for his life to a city gate, and I get winded running to the oven when the timer goes off.

cards.question: The city of refuge is there so the manslayer won't die before he stands trial before the ___.

cards.text: Six cities of refuge in all. And remember, two and a half tribes already have their land across the Jordan, toward the sunrise (Numbers 34:14-15).

cards.question: True or false: All six cities of refuge are in the land of Canaan.
True or false: The six cities of refuge are for Israelites only, not for any foreigner living among them.

cards.text: Then the LORD switches to a whole different kind of killing: someone strikes a person dead with an iron object, a stone of deadly size, or a deadly object of wood. Friend, the most dangerous thing I've ever held is a rolling pin, and I hold it with my MUSTACHE.

cards.question: When someone kills a person with a deadly weapon like that, what does the LORD say must happen to him?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He may flee to a city of refuge
He must pay the family back

cards.question: That murderer must be put to death. Who does the LORD say is to do it?

cards.text: And it's not only about weapons, friend: maliciously pushing someone, or intentionally throwing something at him so that he dies, makes a person a murderer too. Maliciously. Intentionally. Those two words are doing ALL the heavy lifting here.

cards.question: True or false: Striking someone with just a hand, in hostility, so that he dies, still makes a person a murderer.

cards.text: Now flip it around: a sudden push without hostility, something thrown unintentionally, or a heavy stone dropped without looking, by someone who wasn't an enemy and didn't intend to harm him. I've dropped a whole tray of cookies without looking, friend, so I know that sinking feeling right down to my gold base.

cards.question: When it happens like that, the ___ must judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood.
The assembly is to ___ the manslayer, keeping him from the hand of the avenger of blood.

cards.text: Then the assembly sends him back to the city of refuge he fled to, and there he has to STAY. This is not a weekend getaway, friend.

cards.question: How long must the manslayer live in his city of refuge?

cards.text: But what if the manslayer goes outside the limits of his city, and the avenger of blood finds him out there? Friend, I stayed put for YEARS in a junk drawer, and nobody even had to ask me.

cards.question: True or false: If the avenger of blood kills the manslayer outside his city of refuge, the avenger is guilty of bloodshed.
True or false: Once the high priest dies, the manslayer may return to the land he owns.

cards.text: And these rules aren't just for the trip into Canaan. They're a statutory ordinance for the generations to come, wherever Israel lives.

cards.question: Before a murderer can be put to death, how many witnesses does it take?

cards.text: Now, could somebody just pay their way out of all this? Like waving cash at the parking ticket on your windshield and hoping it peels itself right off?

cards.question: What does the LORD say about taking a ransom for a murderer who deserves to die?

answers.text: Accept it if the family agrees
Accept it once a priest approves

cards.question: True or false: A manslayer in a city of refuge can pay a ransom to go home before the high priest dies.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells them not to pollute the land where they live, because bloodshed pollutes the land.

cards.question: For land where blood has been shed, how can atonement be made?

answers.text: By the blood of the one who shed it
By an offering of a spotless lamb
By leaving the land empty for a year

cards.question: Don't defile the land, the LORD says, because He ___ among the Israelites.

findings.problem: The right answer, forty-eight, is stated in Numbers 35:7, but the card cites Numbers 35:6-7. Verse 6 only supplies the forty-two that the question already gives. The question also just asks the baker to add 6 and 42, which is a math check and not a moment of the passage.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The question gives both numbers and asks for their sum, so it tests arithmetic rather than anything that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The avenger first appears here as 'the avenger', with no word on who he is. The passage never says who the avenger of blood is (for example, a relative of the one killed), so any explanation would come from outside the passage. The walkthrough also says hard words get a dictionary pop-up instead of card words.
findings.question: Does the 'New people' rule (say simply who they are) apply to a role like the avenger of blood that the passage doesn't explain? If so, what may Papa Dorin say about who he is, and with what reference? Or is the dictionary pop-up enough?

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the main sentence, 'Maliciously.', 'Intentionally.' and 'Those two words are doing ALL the heavy lifting here.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'When it happens like that', which points back to the accidental-killing cases on card 6. That card is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say what situation it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks how many witnesses it takes. Two of the answers are counts ('More than one witness', 'A single witness'), but 'Only the avenger's word' is a different kind of answer. It also overlaps with 'a single witness'.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. The core action is paying money to get out of a penalty, and paying a parking ticket really does settle it. 'Waving cash at the parking ticket' and 'hoping it peels itself right off' blends two muddled images, and a stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
